The *Pabhaṅkarattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Therāpadāna* within the Pali Tipiṭaka (designated as Tha Ap 338) [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the collection detailing the past meritorious deeds and spiritual biographies of senior Buddhist monks. SuttaCentral notes translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis via DharmaNexus reveals extensive textual reuse within Pali literature, identifying 129 matching passages distributed across 21 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali correspondences occur in the first part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (28 matches, including §9.1–10.4), as well as other Apadāna poems such as the *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430, §6.4–10.4), the *Uttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 558), and the *Tikaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 503) [DharmaNexus]. Verses are also closely shared with structurally adjacent *Therāpadāna* texts, including the *Tiṇakuṭidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 339) and the *Dhammasavaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 341) across segments §20.1–22.1, along with the *Ukkhittapadumiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 342) and several *Therīapadāna* texts [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments suggest formulaic parallels in the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2) and the Sanskrit *Mañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, although these reflect algorithmic text reuse rather than established direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
